title: Vulkan fallback can exceed heap capacity, mask fatal errors and select feature-dependent memory
body:
Confirmed on main `fc22df05140b15ed6d764beabd12a1b807011bc5` with public-constructor ash function-table stubs:

- Shared blocks are not capped to their selected physical heap. A valid small resource on a heap smaller than the configured minimum can issue `vkAllocateMemory` with allocationSize greater than heap.size (VUID-vkAllocateMemory-pAllocateInfo-01713).
- Fallback does not consistently check the fallback heap and can retry the same memory type. Fatal allocation/mapping errors can be hidden by fallback; host-memory exhaustion is not consistently classified as recoverable.
- Automatic selection can reach enumerated DEVICE_COHERENT_AMD types without knowing whether deviceCoherentMemory was enabled. Enumeration does not establish feature enablement.

The allocation-count defect already has #125; the prepared fix also guards this allocator's owned count, including dedicated and cached blocks, while permitting reuse at the limit. Other allocators/native allocations still require coordination by the caller.

[Independent fix and ten regressions](https://github.com/simzy39/gpu-allocator/tree/fix/vulkan-allocation-contracts). Nine regressions fail on main, all ten pass with the fix. Strict std/no_std Clippy and Rust 1.71 std / 1.81 no_std consumers pass. The existing growth/cache policy is preserved, so #322 remains separate. AMD device-coherent types are excluded because the allocator has no enablement input.

Normal failed vkMapMemory calls already release native memory on main; this is not a failed-map leak report. Null-success and first-suballocation cleanup are defensive hardening. [Native allocation contract](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkAllocateMemory.html). Agent-assisted investigation, implementation and report.
